summary: A0040 is an annotation-only SUPERSEDE that adds a single 'superseded_by: T112' field to T109's record in todo/config.yaml. The candidate diff is exactly four files: todo/amendments/A0040/{request.json,planner-001.json,impacts.json} (new lane files) and one inserted line in todo/config.yaml at the T109 record (after task_file, before attempt). No other path is touched. Scope (check 1) is satisfied: SUPERSEDE permits todo/config.yaml as the sole edit, and the candidate touches only the lane files plus that one config line. Frozen state (check 2) holds: the controller's finish-amendment drift check uses _without_amendment_owned_config_fields (tools/workflow/core.py:869), which strips the superseded_by field from both the base and candidate configs (core.py:875), so the single-line annotation is precisely what the drift check is designed to allow. The only pre-existing task that changes is T109, and only via the new superseded_by field; T109.lifecycle/DELIVERED, claimed, depends_on, replaces, task_file, attempt, base_commit, candidate_commit, approved_commit and latest_review are all unchanged (verified by reading the T109 record at config.yaml:1309-1332 against the diff). Existing contracts are byte-identical (check 3): the candidate diff against todo/phases/ is empty, including T109.md. No gate is weakened (check 4): no Must not clause, acceptance criterion, test assertion, safety, risk, promotion or precision rule is touched. Coherence (check 5) holds: T109.superseded_by=T112 agrees with T112.replaces=["T109"] (config.yaml:1385-1387) and T112.depends_on includes "T109" (config.yaml:1383); T112 is DELIVERED with approved_commit 40ad3a25..., satisfying the validator's APPROVED-successor requirement at core.py:1088-1103. Nothing live is left stale (check 6): affected_existing_tasks is empty, which is the correct positive claim because the six prior consumers (T073, T084, T087, T107, T108, T110) were repointed away from T109 by A0030/A0032-A0036/A0039 and their depends_on arrays no longer mention T109. The four remaining indirect references in T088/T103/T096/T111 are descriptive text about the historical T109→T110→T111 chain and the compatibility adapter; SUPERSEDE per todo/WORKFLOW.md is annotation-only and cannot rewrite those contracts, so the planner's 'T109 remains readable as a historical read-only predecessor' framing is the only correct one and retargeting those contracts is correctly left to author responsibility under their own future CONTRACT amendments. Implementation/data/operational impact (check 7) is properly marked not-applicable across all nine dimensions: SUPERSEDE edits no Intent, Spec, contract text, source, test, schema, on-disk artifact, RPC endpoint, signing surface or permission. Consumer and migration closure (check 8) holds: T109's contract, dependencies, attempt, base/candidate/approved commits and review-004.json evidence remain frozen at their recorded values; T112 already lists T109 in depends_on and replaces, so successor self-identification is wired; and the four residual indirect consumer references are descriptive narrative rather than active task dependencies, so no retire-before-repoint ordering risk exists. Plan validity (check 9) passes: 'python3 -m tools.workflow validate' returns {"status": "OK"}; the dependency graph remains acyclic because T109 is annotated as superseded rather than removed; and the plan-structure revision line in todo/README.md is unaffected because SUPERSEDE does not change plan structure. Provenance and secrets (check 10): no external facts, URLs, credentials or environment values are introduced. Authority non-escalation (check 11) is satisfied: the candidate does not touch tools/workflow/, .claude/, todo/schemas/, src/, tests/, .github/, or any future tools/workflow/core_policy.py; the only permanent-blacklist item it could plausibly touch is config.yaml, and that touch is limited to a single SUPERSEDE-permitted annotation line. Trusted-base review (check 12) holds: the candidate does not edit the validator, the schema, the reviewer prompt, or its own role definition; the controller's review worktree is created from base 81dae34..., so any attempt by the candidate to rewrite its own validation surface would not apply to this review. One minor cosmetic note (not a defect): the planner rationale text refers to T109's contract as 'frozen at base 6c31778'; that hash is the V1 baseline commit and the underlying claim that T109.md is unchanged is true (the diff is empty), but the precise base_commit recorded for T109 is 0ef2ce08.... This is a wording imprecision in the rationale prose and does not affect any reviewable claim or the amendment's semantics. All twelve checks are satisfied.
